title: Preparation and Performance Characterization of Superhydrophobic Ni-Diamond Composite Coatings by Magnetic Field-Assisted Jet Electrodeposition
content: The complex and harsh marine environment, combined with the synergistic effect of severe corrosion induced by high salinity and marine biofouling, readily causes corro-sion damage to metallic materials, thereby accelerating their failure process. This study adopted a two-step method via magnetic field‑assisted jet electrodeposition to fabri-cate nickel‑diamond composite coatings. In the first step, a longitudinal dendritic cluster structure was prepared by optimizing the magnetic field intensity and the nickel grain size during jet electrodeposition. Subsequently, the composite coating was obtained by electrodepositing nickel with diamond particles. Finally, superhydropho-bicity was achieved through low‑surface‑energy modification. Experimental results showed that with a nickel particle diameter of 2 μm and a magnetic field intensity of 150 mT, the coating exhibited favorable comprehensive performance, yielding a cluster structure with a water contact angle of 154.9°. The corrosion resistance was character-ized by a self‑corrosion current density of 1.301 × 10⁻⁷ A/cm² and a self‑corrosion po-tential of −0.193 V. Moreover, the incorporation of diamond particles significantly im-proved the wear resistance, as evidenced by a dry friction coefficient as low as 0.145 on the coating surface. This study provides an efficient and rapid laboratory-scale route for fabricating superhydrophobic surfaces with a low friction coefficient, offering a ba-sis for further evaluation toward marine engineering applications.
